standards.text: the study of electrostatics is essential in explaining the electrical nature of matter; and
the relationships among electrical quantities, such as electric potential difference (voltage), current, and resistance are important in maintaining efficient and safe electrical systems;

magnetism is a property of certain materials arising from the alignment of atomic magnetic domains, and that natural magnetic phenomena such as Earth's magnetic field influence navigation and living organisms;

a moving electric charge changes the characteristics of the space around it by establishing a magnetic field in addition to its electric field, enabling moving charges to interact through magnetic forces; and
the study of electromagnetism explains the relationship between electric and magnetic fields, electromagnetic induction, and the technologies that make modern life possible.

The learners can demonstrate their understanding of the principles of electrostatics and current electricity by using theoretical and experimental approaches to solve context-rich problems and situations involving these branches of Physics.
The learners can explain the principles of electromagnetism through theoretical and experimental approaches and can recognize their significance in electrical devices.

competencies.text: explain the nature of charge and different charging processes;
calculate the total electrostatic force on a point charge due to a system of charges in one-dimensional or two-dimensional spaces;
describe the nature of the electric field due to a single point charge;
determine the magnitude and direction of the electrostatic force on a static point charge in a region of a constant electric field;
explain the factors affecting electric potential and its distinction from electric potential energy;
design and conduct an experiment to graphically validate the relationship among current, resistance, and voltage in direct-current circuits (series, parallel, and combination) as stated in Ohm’s Law;
explain how the geometric properties of a capacitor, particularly plate area and plate separation, affect capacitance;
differentiate series and parallel capacitor configurations and describe their effects on the circuit’s total capacitance; and
solve problems involving Ohm’s Law, resistance, and capacitance in a circuit.
describe how the alignment of magnetic domains in materials produces magnetism and how this relates to magnetic and non-magnetic materials;
explain the characteristics and significance of Earth’s magnetic field, including its role in navigation and its uses and effects on living organisms;
calculate the magnetic force acting on a moving electric charge and a current-carrying conductor in a uniform magnetic field;
interpret diagrams and relationships describing the magnetic fields produced by current-carrying conductors and solenoids.;
explain how different factors affect the magnitude of an induced electromotive force based on Faraday’s law of electromagnetic induction;
interpret Lenz’s Law because of the conservation of energy in electromagnetic induction;
analyze context-rich problems using Faraday’s law of electromagnetic induction;
explain the difference between direct current (DC) and alternating current (AC) and their applications;
explain the working principles of electric motors, electric generators, and transformers using electromagnetic induction; and
describe how electromagnetic induction is applied in technologies such as maglev trains, metal detectors, traffic sensors, and magnetic cards.
